newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares drop despite Arab Bank demand.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares drop despite Arab Bank demand.

text.p: Shares on the Jordanian stock exchange dropped 0.29 percent at the end of weekly trade on Wednesday despite strong demand by Arab Bank, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index slipped 0.45 points to 156.29 points in high turnover of 1.29 million dinars ($1.82 million).

Arab Bank, a main beneficiary of a new companies law currently being approved by parliament, rose 1.00 dinars to 262 dinars. The stock's large 635,960 dinars turnover alone accounted for nearly half the daily volume.
"There was intensive buying on some companies for non-Jordanian parties...demand has shrunk to a limited number of stocks," said one broker.
Despite rises in a handful of firms, most of the blue-chip stocks dropped on Wednesday as falling shares outnumbered gainers by 23 to seven.

Shares rose on Saturday to a 14-month high, boosted by a recent parliamentary decision to scrap a 15 percent tax on transfers of cash from reserves into paid-up capital. Brokers say foreign buying also propelled the official index higher.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange shed 0.14 percent to 82.52 points.
